items.description: jq's // operator treats false as empty, so `.telemetry // true` returns true for an explicit {"telemetry": false} — the one value the setting exists to express. README:11 documents false as the way to disable the telemetry guard, and hooks/guard.sh only blocks when telemetry_enabled prints false, so the opt-out silently never takes effect. The correct test is `.telemetry == false`.

Both helpers call sha256sum with no fallback. sha256sum is not present on a stock macOS, where the equivalent is `shasum -a 256`, and README:3 states the plugin runs on macOS. Every cache key computation fails there with command not found.

The log is append-only JSONL, and `jq -c` over it aborts the whole query on the first malformed line — one truncated append makes every prior learning unreadable rather than skipping the bad record. A scan of an append-only log reads it as raw lines and parses defensively (`jq -Rc 'fromjson?'`).
`tail -r` reverses only on BSD/macOS; on the Linux the README also claims support for, tail has no -r and the call fails. The portable pair is `tail -r` on BSD and `tac` on GNU, chosen at runtime.

The substitution rewrites every occurrence of the bare basename anywhere in a line, so a rename of plan.md also rewrites the tail of `archive/plan.md` and any prose mention of the word. A path-rename sweep has to exclude a preceding path separator, or anchor on the full path.

The retry limit 3 is stated in four places: lib/config.sh:15 as the code default, skills/audit/SKILL.md:20, README.md:12 in the settings table, and README.md:14 again in prose. One value, four homes, no single source — they agree today and drift on the first change.
